transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

My head feels foggy and I can’t focus long enough to figure out my bills or make decisions about work anymore. I'm just having a really hard time keeping track of anything right now and it's getting overwhelming.

Have you noticed these difficulties with focus and memory starting suddenly after a specific medical illness, injury, or change in medication, or have they been developing more gradually over a long period?

No, I haven't had any head injuries, sicknesses, or new medicines lately. This brain fog and trouble focusing got really bad over the last month after my work hours were cut and the bills started piling up. I’ve had times where I felt down coming and going for several months before that, but it's never been this hard to think.
Over the past two years, have you felt low or down for more days than not, or was there a period where you felt mostly like your normal self before this recent decline?

No, it hasn't been a constant low for two years; these down feelings were just coming and going for several months before my hours got cut. Before this bad crash, I definitely had times where I felt like my normal self, doing my lakefront walks and building my models, and even a brief stretch where I felt strangely high and wired.
During that brief stretch when you felt 'high and wired,' did you find that you needed much less sleep than usual, felt unusually energetic, or found yourself talking much faster than normal?

Yes, I only slept about three hours a night but still woke up feeling completely wired and rested. I had so much energy that I was constantly pacing and felt like I had to keep moving. I was also talking incredibly fast, rambling on about my plans so much that my cousin couldn't even get a word in.
During that period when you felt high and wired, did these symptoms last for at least a week, or did they resolve sooner than that?
No, it didn't last a full week. It was just a brief stretch for a few days before I crashed back down into feeling completely depressed and exhausted.

During those few days when you were feeling high, wired, and sleeping very little, did your behavior become so intense that it caused noticeable problems at work or in your relationships, or did others express serious concern about your actions?

During that high time, I did snap at people if they questioned me and talked my cousin's ear off without letting her get a word in. But while she noticed I was acting unlike myself then, the major problems like missing shifts and falling behind on rent didn't really hit until I crashed into this low, foggy state.
Have you experienced other episodes of feeling 'high and wired' like that in the past, or was that the only time you've ever felt that way?

That was actually the only time I ever remember feeling that high and wired or unusually driven. I've had times where I felt down and depressed coming and going for several months before, but I never experienced that kind of extreme energy or racing thoughts until this past month.

During your current period of feeling down, have you experienced any symptoms like moving or speaking much more slowly than usual, or feeling completely unable to experience pleasure in the activities you used to enjoy?

Yes, I feel like I’m moving underwater now, taking forever just to get dressed or wash the dishes because my body feels so heavy. I've also completely lost interest in walking by the lake or building my model cars, and now I just lie on the couch staring at the TV without caring about anything.

During this current period of feeling down, have you experienced any symptoms like delusions, hallucinations, or a complete inability to function in your daily life, such as being unable to eat or care for your basic personal hygiene?

No, I haven't seen or heard things that aren't there, and I don't have any delusions. But my functioning is extremely bad—while it's not a complete total shutdown, I have to force myself to eat just one sandwich a day, and taking forever to do basic things like get dressed or wash dishes has caused me to miss work shifts and fall behind on rent.
